notes: Full manufacturer datasheet (Axis Communications, doc T10139377/EN/M22.2/2501) was read directly. AXIS C1310-E is an outdoor network horn speaker with an integrated 7 W Class D amplifier and built-in microphone — there are no external analog audio jacks; audio is delivered entirely over the network (SIP/VAPIX/AAC/G.711/etc.), so no audio connector ports are listed. Power arrives solely via PoE on the RJ45 port (802.3af/802.3at Type 1 Class 3, 12.95 W max) — no separate mains or DC-barrel input exists on this unit. Ethernet grade set to eth-100m because the datasheet specifies "RJ45 10BASE-T/100BASE-TX PoE" (Fast Ethernet only, not Gigabit). The 4-pin 2.5 mm terminal block is generic GPIO (virtual/external input + output for triggers, e.g. door contact or relay) rather than a bandwidth-graded connector; "euroblock" was chosen as the closest connector id in the allowed list for a pluggable screw-terminal block — no grade applies. Note: Axis has since released a "C1310-E Mk II" successor; specs above are for the original (non-Mk II) C1310-E.

ports.name: Network
ports.note: 10BASE-T/100BASE-TX; also the PoE power input (IEEE 802.3af/802.3at Type 1 Class 3, max 12.95 W) — device has no separate DC power jack.

ports.name: I/O (Input)
ports.note: One of two contacts on the shared 4-pin, 2.5 mm pitch terminal block (1 in + 1 out, GPIO-style alarm/relay I/O, not audio-grade).

ports.name: I/O (Output)
ports.note: One of two contacts on the shared 4-pin, 2.5 mm pitch terminal block (1 in + 1 out, GPIO-style alarm/relay I/O, not audio-grade).
